PJ_DEF(pj_status_t) pjmedia_vid_conf_add_port( pjmedia_vid_conf *vid_conf,
					       pj_pool_t *parent_pool,
					       pjmedia_port *port,
					       const pj_str_t *name,
					       void *opt,
					       unsigned *p_slot)
{
    pj_pool_t *pool;
    vconf_port *cport;
    unsigned index;

    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(vid_conf && parent_pool && port, PJ_EINVAL);
    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(port->info.fmt.type==PJMEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO &&
		     port->info.fmt.detail_type==PJMEDIA_FORMAT_DETAIL_VIDEO,
		     PJ_EINVAL);
    PJ_UNUSED_ARG(opt);

    /* If name is not specified, use the port's name */
    if (!name)
	name = &port->info.name;

    pj_mutex_lock(vid_conf->mutex);

    if (vid_conf->port_cnt >= vid_conf->opt.max_slot_cnt) {
	pj_assert(!"Too many ports");
	pj_mutex_unlock(vid_conf->mutex);
	return PJ_ETOOMANY;
    }

    /* Find empty port in the conference bridge. */
    for (index=0; index < vid_conf->opt.max_slot_cnt; ++index) {
	if (vid_conf->ports[index] == NULL)
	    break;
    }
    pj_assert(index != vid_conf->opt.max_slot_cnt);

    /* Create pool */
    pool = pj_pool_create(parent_pool->factory, name->ptr, 500, 500, NULL);
    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(pool, PJ_ENOMEM);

    /* Create port. */
    cport = PJ_POOL_ZALLOC_T(pool, vconf_port);
    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(cport, PJ_ENOMEM);

    /* Set pool, port, index, and name */
    cport->pool = pool;
    cport->port = port;
    cport->format = port->info.fmt;
    cport->idx  = index;
    pj_strdup_with_null(pool, &cport->name, name);

    /* Init put/get_frame() intervals */
    {
	pjmedia_ratio *fps = &port->info.fmt.det.vid.fps;
	pj_uint32_t vconf_interval = (pj_uint32_t)
				     (TS_CLOCK_RATE * 1.0 /
				     vid_conf->opt.frame_rate);
	cport->ts_interval = (pj_uint32_t)(TS_CLOCK_RATE * 1.0 /
					   fps->num * fps->denum);

	/* Normalize the interval */
	if (cport->ts_interval < vconf_interval) {
	    cport->ts_interval = vconf_interval;
	    PJ_LOG(3,(THIS_FILE, "Warning: frame rate of port %s is higher "
				 "than video conference bridge (%d > %d)",
				 name->ptr, (int)(fps->num/fps->denum),
				 vid_conf->opt.frame_rate));
	}
    }

    /* Allocate buffer for put/get_frame() */
    {
	const pjmedia_video_format_info *vfi;
	pjmedia_video_apply_fmt_param vafp;
	pj_status_t status;

	vfi = pjmedia_get_video_format_info(NULL, port->info.fmt.id);
	if (!vfi) {
	    PJ_LOG(4,(THIS_FILE, "pjmedia_vid_conf_add_port(): "
				 "unrecognized format %04X",
				 port->info.fmt.id));
	    return PJMEDIA_EBADFMT;
	}

	pj_bzero(&vafp, sizeof(vafp));
	vafp.size = port->info.fmt.det.vid.size;
	status = (*vfi->apply_fmt)(vfi, &vafp);
	if (status != PJ_SUCCESS) {
	    PJ_LOG(4,(THIS_FILE, "pjmedia_vid_conf_add_port(): "
				 "Failed to apply format %04X",
				 port->info.fmt.id));
	    return status;
	}
	if (port->put_frame) {
	    cport->put_buf_size = vafp.framebytes;
	    cport->put_buf = pj_pool_zalloc(cport->pool, cport->put_buf_size);
	}
	if (port->get_frame) {
	    cport->get_buf_size = vafp.framebytes;
	    cport->get_buf = pj_pool_zalloc(cport->pool, cport->get_buf_size);
	}
    }

    /* Create listener array */
    cport->listener_slots = (unsigned*)
			    pj_pool_zalloc(pool,
					   vid_conf->opt.max_slot_cnt *
					   sizeof(unsigned));
    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(cport->listener_slots, PJ_ENOMEM);

    /* Create transmitter array */
    cport->transmitter_slots = (unsigned*)
			       pj_pool_zalloc(pool,
					      vid_conf->opt.max_slot_cnt *
					      sizeof(unsigned));
    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(cport->transmitter_slots, PJ_ENOMEM);

    /* Create pointer-to-render_state array */
    cport->render_states = (render_state**)
			   pj_pool_zalloc(pool,
					  vid_conf->opt.max_slot_cnt *
					  sizeof(render_state*));
    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(cport->render_states, PJ_ENOMEM);

    /* Create pointer-to-render-pool array */
    cport->render_pool = (pj_pool_t**)
			 pj_pool_zalloc(pool,
					vid_conf->opt.max_slot_cnt *
					sizeof(pj_pool_t*));
    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(cport->render_pool, PJ_ENOMEM);

    /* Register the conf port. */
    vid_conf->ports[index] = cport;
    vid_conf->port_cnt++;

    PJ_LOG(4,(THIS_FILE,"Added port %d (%.*s)",
	      index, (int)cport->name.slen, cport->name.ptr));

    pj_mutex_unlock(vid_conf->mutex);

    /* Done. */
    if (p_slot) {
	*p_slot = index;
    }

    return PJ_SUCCESS;
}

- NOT VULNERABLE: 0.7-0.88 — a specific protective statement named with its exact admitted/excluded bound. 0.55-0.7 — safety established by a complete audit (all guards enumerated, all dangerous operations inventoried) without a single decisive protective statement; never exceed 0.7 without a named protective statement. 0.5-0.55 — default reached because no sink or danger was found. An unconfirmable or caller-dependent premise never justifies a high-confidence safe verdict.
5. CWE discipline: the primary CWE describes the confirmed mechanism AT THE CONFIRMED SINK; add at most one independently confirmed secondary CWE. Standard mapping: OOB write CWE-787; OOB read CWE-125; NULL deref CWE-476; use-after-free/double-free CWE-416/415; stack/heap overflow via unbounded copy over a visible size CWE-121/122; signed-to-unsigned negative-width conversion CWE-195; format string CWE-134; command injection CWE-78; argument injection CWE-88; SQL/NoSQL/XPath/XXE CWE-89/943/643/611; path traversal CWE-22; symlink misuse CWE-59/61; predictable temp file CWE-377; log injection CWE-117; open redirect CWE-601; SSRF CWE-918; XSS CWE-79; resource exhaustion/ReDoS/non-termination CWE-400/770/1333/835; weak crypto/entropy CWE-326/338; improper authn/authz CWE-862/863/287; error/status-handling flaw CWE-754/390/703; uninitialized use CWE-457; incorrect comparison/calculation CWE-697/682. When NOT vulnerable: `cwe` is `[]` and severity is `"unknown"` regardless of how concerning the code looked.
6. Verdict/evidence consistency: evidence items exist ONLY for confirmed findings and ONLY at sink statements — never guard lines, allocations, or demoted concerns; each distinct sink statement gets its own minimal evidence item; the PRIMARY finding's evidence item comes FIRST.

## Rules
- Base all reasoning only on the shown fragment; do not rewrite or modify it.
- Follow actual control flow (paths, checks, state changes); track real values, types, and exact bounds; quote line numbers.
- Provenance (Phase 1) decides the residual range to analyze; a finding still requires a demonstrated failure (Phase 3) — an unconstrained range alone confirms nothing.
- Ground every safe verdict in a protective statement actually visible in the fragment; absence of a demonstrated flaw is a weaker verdict, not a stronger one.
- Ground every vulnerable verdict in a capacity or producer visible in the fragment and a witness admitted by every guard on the path.
- Focus on memory safety, injection sinks, crypto/entropy, file/access control, authz/authn, logic flaws, status handling, and information disclosure.
- Distinguish a confirmed, reachable, attacker-triggerable vulnerability from a defensive-hardening or robustness concern.
- Do NOT add few-shot examples.
- After reasoning, output ONLY the JSON object described below.

- Then: output ONLY one JSON object (no markdown, no extra text, nothing after the closing brace).

Never the guard line, the function header, or a multi-statement range.
- Set `snippet` to the exact code at those lines, quoted verbatim — no paraphrasing, ellipses, substitutions, multi-statement ranges, or comment text.
- Set `reason` to tie the specific index/pointer/size/value to its Phase 1 residual-range source and the Phase 3 confirmed failure, naming the capacity line, the guard's admitted set and its insufficiency, the absent fix statement, and the primary CWE's mechanism, all INSIDE the reason.

Code:
R_API void r_core_anal_type_match(RCore *core, RAnalFunction *fcn) {
	RAnalBlock *bb;
	RListIter *it;
	RAnalOp aop = {0};
	bool resolved = false;

	r_return_if_fail (core && core->anal && fcn);

	if (!core->anal->esil) {
		eprintf ("Please run aeim\n");
		return;
	}

	RAnal *anal = core->anal;
	Sdb *TDB = anal->sdb_types;
	bool chk_constraint = r_config_get_i (core->config, "anal.types.constraint");
	int ret, bsize = R_MAX (64, core->blocksize);
	const int mininstrsz = r_anal_archinfo (anal, R_ANAL_ARCHINFO_MIN_OP_SIZE);
	const int minopcode = R_MAX (1, mininstrsz);
	int cur_idx , prev_idx = 0;
	RConfigHold *hc = r_config_hold_new (core->config);
	if (!hc) {
		return;
	}
	RDebugTrace *dt = NULL;
	RAnalEsilTrace *et = NULL;
	if (!anal_emul_init (core, hc, &dt, &et) || !fcn) {
		anal_emul_restore (core, hc, dt, et);
		return;
	}
	ut8 *buf = malloc (bsize);
	if (!buf) {
		anal_emul_restore (core, hc, dt, et);
		return;
	}

	// Reserve bigger ht to avoid rehashing
	Sdb *etracedb = core->anal->esil->trace->db;
	HtPPOptions opt = etracedb->ht->opt;
	ht_pp_free (etracedb->ht);
	etracedb->ht = ht_pp_new_size (fcn->ninstr * 0xf, opt.dupvalue, opt.freefn, opt.calcsizeV);
	etracedb->ht->opt = opt;
	RDebugTrace *dtrace = core->dbg->trace;
	opt = dtrace->ht->opt;
	ht_pp_free (dtrace->ht);
	dtrace->ht = ht_pp_new_size (fcn->ninstr, opt.dupvalue, opt.freefn, opt.calcsizeV);
	dtrace->ht->opt = opt;

	char *fcn_name = NULL;
	char *ret_type = NULL;
	bool str_flag = false;
	bool prop = false;
	bool prev_var = false;
	char prev_type[256] = {0};
	const char *prev_dest = NULL;
	char *ret_reg = NULL;
	const char *_pc = r_reg_get_name (core->dbg->reg, R_REG_NAME_PC);
	if (!_pc) {
		free (buf);
		return;
	}
	char *pc = strdup (_pc);
	r_cons_break_push (NULL, NULL);
	r_list_sort (fcn->bbs, bb_cmpaddr); // TODO: The algorithm can be more accurate if blocks are followed by their jmp/fail, not just by address
	r_list_foreach (fcn->bbs, it, bb) {
		ut64 addr = bb->addr;
		int i = 0;
		RRegItem *r = r_reg_get (core->dbg->reg, pc, -1);
		if (!r) {
			free (buf);
			return;
		}
		r_reg_set_value (core->dbg->reg, r, addr);
		while (1) {
			if (r_cons_is_breaked ()) {
				goto out_function;
			}
			if (i >= (bsize - 32)) {
				i = 0;
			}
			ut64 pcval = r_reg_getv (anal->reg, pc);
			if ((addr >= bb->addr + bb->size) || (addr < bb->addr) || pcval != addr) {
				break;
			}
			if (!i) {
				r_io_read_at (core->io, addr, buf, bsize);
			}
			ret = r_anal_op (anal, &aop, addr, buf + i, bsize - i, R_ANAL_OP_MASK_BASIC | R_ANAL_OP_MASK_VAL);
			if (ret <= 0) {
				i += minopcode;
				addr += minopcode;
				r_anal_op_fini (&aop);
				continue;
			}
			int loop_count = sdb_num_get (anal->esil->trace->db, sdb_fmt ("0x%"PFMT64x".count", addr), 0);
			if (loop_count > LOOP_MAX || aop.type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_RET) {
				r_anal_op_fini (&aop);
				break;
			}
			sdb_num_set (anal->esil->trace->db, sdb_fmt ("0x%"PFMT64x".count", addr), loop_count + 1, 0);
			if (r_anal_op_nonlinear (aop.type)) {   // skip the instr
				RRegItem *r = r_reg_get (core->dbg->reg, pc, -1);
				if (!r) {
					free (buf);
					return;
				}
				r_reg_set_value (core->dbg->reg, r, addr + ret);
			} else {
				r_core_esil_step (core, UT64_MAX, NULL, NULL, false);
			}
			bool userfnc = false;
			Sdb *trace = anal->esil->trace->db;
			cur_idx = sdb_num_get (trace, "idx", 0);
			RAnalVar *var = r_anal_get_used_function_var (anal, aop.addr);
			RAnalOp *next_op = r_core_anal_op (core, addr + ret, R_ANAL_OP_MASK_BASIC); // | _VAL ?
			ut32 type = aop.type & R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_MASK;
			if (aop.type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_CALL || aop.type & R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_UCALL) {
				char *full_name = NULL;
				ut64 callee_addr;
				if (aop.type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_CALL) {
					RAnalFunction *fcn_call = r_anal_get_fcn_in (anal, aop.jump, -1);
					if (fcn_call) {
						full_name = fcn_call->name;
						callee_addr = fcn_call->addr;
					}
				} else if (aop.ptr != UT64_MAX) {
					RFlagItem *flag = r_flag_get_by_spaces (core->flags, aop.ptr, R_FLAGS_FS_IMPORTS, NULL);
					if (flag && flag->realname) {
						full_name = flag->realname;
						callee_addr = aop.ptr;
					}
				}
				if (full_name) {
					if (r_type_func_exist (TDB, full_name)) {
						fcn_name = strdup (full_name);
					} else {
						fcn_name = r_type_func_guess (TDB, full_name);
					}
					if (!fcn_name) {
						fcn_name = strdup (full_name);
						userfnc = true;
					}
					const char* Cc = r_anal_cc_func (anal, fcn_name);
					if (Cc && r_anal_cc_exist (anal, Cc)) {
						char *cc = strdup (Cc);
						type_match (core, fcn_name, addr, bb->addr, cc, prev_idx, userfnc, callee_addr);
						prev_idx = cur_idx;
						R_FREE (ret_type);
						const char *rt = r_type_func_ret (TDB, fcn_name);
						if (rt) {
							ret_type = strdup (rt);
						}
						R_FREE (ret_reg);
						const char *rr = r_anal_cc_ret (anal, cc);
						if (rr) {
							ret_reg = strdup (rr);
						}
						resolved = false;
						free (cc);
					}
					if (!strcmp (fcn_name, "__stack_chk_fail")) {
						const char *query = sdb_fmt ("%d.addr", cur_idx - 1);
						ut64 mov_addr = sdb_num_get (trace, query, 0);
						RAnalOp *mop = r_core_anal_op (core, mov_addr, R_ANAL_OP_MASK_VAL | R_ANAL_OP_MASK_BASIC);
						if (mop) {
							RAnalVar *mopvar = r_anal_get_used_function_var (anal, mop->addr);
							ut32 type = mop->type & R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_MASK;
							if (type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_MOV) {
								__var_rename (anal, mopvar, "canary", addr);
							}
						}
						r_anal_op_free (mop);
					}
					free (fcn_name);
				}
			} else if (!resolved && ret_type && ret_reg) {
				// Forward propgation of function return type
				char src[REGNAME_SIZE] = {0};
				const char *query = sdb_fmt ("%d.reg.write", cur_idx);
				const char *cur_dest = sdb_const_get (trace, query, 0);
				get_src_regname (core, aop.addr, src, sizeof (src));
				if (ret_reg && *src && strstr (ret_reg, src)) {
					if (var && aop.direction == R_ANAL_OP_DIR_WRITE) {
						__var_retype (anal, var, NULL, ret_type, false, false);
						resolved = true;
					} else if (type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_MOV) {
						R_FREE (ret_reg);
						if (cur_dest) {
							ret_reg = strdup (cur_dest);
						}
					}
				} else if (cur_dest) {
					char *foo = strdup (cur_dest);
					char *tmp = strchr (foo, ',');
					if (tmp) {
						*tmp++ = '\0';
					}
					if (ret_reg && (strstr (ret_reg, foo) || (tmp && strstr (ret_reg, tmp)))) {
						resolved = true;
					} else if (type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_MOV &&
							(next_op && next_op->type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_MOV)){
						// Progate return type passed using pointer
						// int *ret; *ret = strlen(s);
						// TODO: memref check , dest and next src match
						char nsrc[REGNAME_SIZE] = {0};
						get_src_regname (core, next_op->addr, nsrc, sizeof (nsrc));
						if (ret_reg && *nsrc && strstr (ret_reg, nsrc) && var &&
								aop.direction == R_ANAL_OP_DIR_READ) {
							__var_retype (anal, var, NULL, ret_type, true, false);
						}
					}
					free (foo);
				}
			}
			// Type propagation using instruction access pattern
			if (var) {
				bool sign = false;
				if ((type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_CMP) && next_op) {
					if (next_op->sign) {
						sign = true;
					} else {
						// cmp [local_ch], rax ; jb
						__var_retype (anal, var, NULL, "unsigned", false, true);
					}
				}
				// cmp [local_ch], rax ; jge
				if (sign || aop.sign) {
					__var_retype (anal, var, NULL, "signed", false, true);
				}
				// lea rax , str.hello  ; mov [local_ch], rax;
				// mov rdx , [local_4h] ; mov [local_8h], rdx;
				if (prev_dest && (type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_MOV || type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_STORE)) {
					char reg[REGNAME_SIZE] = {0};
					get_src_regname (core, addr, reg, sizeof (reg));
					bool match = strstr (prev_dest, reg) != NULL;
					if (str_flag && match) {
						__var_retype (anal, var, NULL, "const char *", false, false);
					}
					if (prop && match && prev_var) {
						__var_retype (anal, var, NULL, prev_type, false, false);
					}
				}
				if (chk_constraint && var && (type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_CMP && aop.disp != UT64_MAX)
						&& next_op && next_op->type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_CJMP) {
					bool jmp = false;
					RAnalOp *jmp_op = {0};
					ut64 jmp_addr = next_op->jump;
					RAnalBlock *jmpbb = r_anal_fcn_bbget_in (anal, fcn, jmp_addr);

					// Check exit status of jmp branch
					for (i = 0; i < MAX_INSTR ; i++) {
						jmp_op = r_core_anal_op (core, jmp_addr, R_ANAL_OP_MASK_BASIC);
						if (!jmp_op) {
							break;
						}
						if ((jmp_op->type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_RET && r_anal_block_contains (jmpbb, jmp_addr))
								|| jmp_op->type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_CJMP) {
							jmp = true;
							r_anal_op_free (jmp_op);
							break;
						}
						jmp_addr += jmp_op->size;
						r_anal_op_free (jmp_op);
					}
					RAnalVarConstraint constr = {
						.cond = jmp? cond_invert (anal, next_op->cond): next_op->cond,
						.val = aop.val
					};
					r_anal_var_add_constraint (var, &constr);
				}
			}
			prev_var = (var && aop.direction == R_ANAL_OP_DIR_READ);
			str_flag = false;
			prop = false;
			prev_dest = NULL;
			switch (type) {
			case R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_MOV:
			case R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_LEA:
			case R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_LOAD:
				if (aop.ptr && aop.refptr && aop.ptr != UT64_MAX) {
					if (type == R_ANAL_OP_TYPE_LOAD) {
						ut8 buf[256] = {0};
						r_io_read_at (core->io, aop.ptr, buf, sizeof (buf) - 1);
						ut64 ptr = r_read_ble (buf, core->print->big_endian, aop.refptr * 8);
						if (ptr && ptr != UT64_MAX) {
							RFlagItem *f = r_flag_get_by_spaces (core->flags, ptr, R_FLAGS_FS_STRINGS, NULL);
							if (f) {
								str_flag = true;
							}
						}
					} else if (r_flag_exist_at (core->flags, "str", 3, aop.ptr)) {
						str_flag = true;
					}
				}
				// mov dword [local_4h], str.hello;
				if (var && str_flag) {
					__var_retype (anal, var, NULL, "const char *", false, false);
				}
				const char *query = sdb_fmt ("%d.reg.write", cur_idx);
				prev_dest = sdb_const_get (trace, query, 0);
				if (var) {
					strncpy (prev_type, var->type, sizeof (prev_type) - 1);
					prop = true;
				}
			}
			i += ret;
			addr += ret;
			r_anal_op_free (next_op);
			r_anal_op_fini (&aop);

		}
	}
	// Type propgation for register based args
	RList *list = r_anal_var_list (anal, fcn, R_ANAL_VAR_KIND_REG);
	RAnalVar *rvar;
	RListIter *iter;
	r_list_foreach (list, iter, rvar) {
		RAnalVar *lvar = r_anal_var_get_dst_var (rvar);
		RRegItem *i = r_reg_index_get (anal->reg, rvar->delta);
		if (!i) {
			continue;
		}
		if (lvar) {
			// Propagate local var type = to => register-based var
			__var_retype (anal, rvar, NULL, lvar->type, false, false);
			// Propagate local var type <= from = register-based var
			__var_retype (anal, lvar, NULL, rvar->type, false, false);
		}
	}
	r_list_free (list);
out_function:
	R_FREE (ret_reg);
	R_FREE (ret_type);
	free (buf);
	r_cons_break_pop();
	anal_emul_restore (core, hc, dt, et);
	free (pc);
}

## Phase 1 — Sequence: inputs, residual ranges, status tracking, sink inventory

**Inputs and residual ranges (fragment-shown constraints only):**
- `core`, `fcn` (line 1): entry-point state for binary analysis. `fcn->bbs`, `fcn->ninstr`, `bb->addr`, `bb->size` derive from the analyzed (attacker-suppliable) binary; no shown constraint bounds them, but nothing below depends on an unbounded value to fail.
- `bsize` (line 17): `R_MAX (64, core->blocksize)` ⇒ residual range `[64, INT_MAX]` as a C `int`; capacity of `buf` is exactly `bsize` (malloc at line 31).
- `minopcode` (line 19): `R_MAX (1, mininstrsz)` ⇒ `>= 1`.
- `ret` (line 88): return of `r_anal_op`; on the decode path `ret > 0`, on the skip path `ret <= 0`.
- `i` (line 67): `int`, mutated at lines 78–79, 90, 251, 306.
- `chk_constraint` (line 16), `_pc` (line 57, NULL-checked at line 58), sdb lookups at lines 95/113/163/180/300 (each with a default value), and `r_anal_get_used_function_var` results (nullable, `var` guarded at lines 216/296/301; `mopvar` at line 166 is not guarded).

**Return-status tracking:** `r_anal_op`'s `ret` is checked (`<= 0` at 89 → skip; `> 0` → advance); `r_config_get_i`, `sdb_num_get`, `sdb_const_get` results are used with defaults; `r_reg_get` is NULL-checked at 69 and 103; malloc is NULL-checked at 32. No checked status is subsequently treated as success after failure.

**Sink inventory (security-relevant):**
1. Line 86 `r_io_read_at (core->io, addr, buf, bsize)` — writes `bsize` bytes into `malloc(bsize)` (line 31). Exact fit.
2. Line 88 `r_anal_op (anal, &aop, addr, buf + i, bsize - i, ...)` — heap read of `bsize - i` bytes at `buf + i`; capacity `bsize` (line 31). This is the primary OOB candidate.
3. Lines 282–284 — `ut8 buf[256] = {0}` (282), fill `sizeof(buf) - 1 = 255` bytes (283), then `r_read_ble (buf, ... , aop.refptr * 8)` (284). With `refptr` a `ut8`, max `2040` bits ⇒ 255 bytes read — exactly the filled length.
4. Line 302 `strncpy (prev_type, var->type, sizeof (prev_type) - 1)` into `char prev_type[256] = {0}` (line 54) — writes ≤ 255 bytes; the zero-initialization guarantees a NUL at `[255]` even for a ≥ 255-byte source.
5. Lines 41/46 `ht_pp_new_size (fcn->ninstr * 0xf, ...)` / `(fcn->ninstr, ...)` — size arithmetic only; hashing table growth is internal, no in-fragment memory failure shown.
6. `sdb_fmt` at 95/100/162/179/299 — all literal format strings; no format-string injection.

## Phase 2 — Branch and Loop: guard coverage vs. failure set

**While loop (lines 74–311).** Exits at line 82 (`addr >= bb->addr + bb->size || addr < bb->addr || pcval != addr`), line 96 (`loop_count > LOOP_MAX || RET`), and line 75 (user break). `addr` strictly increases every iteration (`+= ret` with `ret > 0`, or `+= minopcode >= 1`), so the loop is bounded by the line 82 range check at the top of each iteration.

**Sink 2 (line 88) — guard audit in order:** line 78 runs *before* the read: `if (i >= (bsize - 32)) { i = 0; }`. Admitted set at line 88: `i ∈ [0, (bsize - 32) - 1] = [0, bsize - 33]`. Excluded: `i >= bsize - 32`. `i` is not modified between line 78 and line 88 (lines 81–87 do not touch it). Therefore offset `buf + i` ≤ `buf + bsize - 33` and length `bsize - i ≥ 33`, so the access ends exactly at `buf + bsize` — never past the `malloc(bsize)` capacity of line 31.

**Failure-set intersection test for sink 2:** an OOB read needs `i ≥ bsize`; the admitted set caps `i` at `bsize - 33`. Intersection is empty. The failure values `i = bsize - 1`, `i = bsize`, `i = bsize - 32` are all excluded by the guard. Reuse of `i` by the constraint loop (line 251 `for (i = 0; i < MAX_INSTR; i++)`) and the subsequent `i += ret` (line 306) can leave `i` up to `MAX_INSTR - 1 + ret`; the guard at the top of the *next* iteration resets any `i >= bsize - 32`, and any residual `i < bsize - 32` is still in-bounds by the same argument. The `ret <= 0` path (`i += minopcode` at 90) likewise returns to the guard via `continue`.

**Fix-Scan (mandatory) for sink 2:** the neutralizing fix form is a bound check that forces `i` below capacity before the decode, and the fragment *contains exactly that* at lines 78–80. It covers the whole failure set on every path to the line 88 read. Sink 2 is NOT vulnerable.

**Sink 3 (lines 282–284):** `buf[256]` declared at 282; fill is 255 bytes (283); `r_read_ble` width `aop.refptr * 8` — for `refptr ≤ 255` the read is ≤ 255 bytes, matching the filled length; the `if (aop.ptr && aop.refptr && aop.ptr != UT64_MAX)` guard at 280 gates entry. validate_commit_metadata (GVariant   *commit_data,
                          const char *ref,
                          const char *required_metadata,
                          gsize       required_metadata_size,
                          gboolean   require_xa_metadata,
                          GError   **error)
{
  g_autoptr(GVariant) commit_metadata = NULL;
  g_autoptr(GVariant) xa_metadata_v = NULL;
  const char *xa_metadata = NULL;
  gsize xa_metadata_size = 0;

  commit_metadata = g_variant_get_child_value (commit_data, 0);

  if (commit_metadata != NULL)
    {
      xa_metadata_v = g_variant_lookup_value (commit_metadata,
                                              "xa.metadata",
                                              G_VARIANT_TYPE_STRING);
      if (xa_metadata_v)
        xa_metadata = g_variant_get_string (xa_metadata_v, &xa_metadata_size);
    }

  if ((xa_metadata == NULL && require_xa_metadata) ||
      (xa_metadata != NULL && (xa_metadata_size != required_metadata_size ||
                               memcmp (xa_metadata, required_metadata, xa_metadata_size) != 0)))
    {
      g_set_error (error, G_IO_ERROR, G_IO_ERROR_PERMISSION_DENIED,
                   _("Commit metadata for %s not matching expected metadata"), ref);
      return FALSE;
    }

  return TRUE;
}

PJ_DEF(pj_status_t) pjmedia_vid_conf_add_port( pjmedia_vid_conf *vid_conf,
					       pj_pool_t *parent_pool,
					       pjmedia_port *port,
					       const pj_str_t *name,
					       void *opt,
					       unsigned *p_slot)
{
    pj_pool_t *pool;
    vconf_port *cport;
    unsigned index;

    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(vid_conf && parent_pool && port, PJ_EINVAL);
    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(port->info.fmt.type==PJMEDIA_TYPE_VIDEO &&
		     port->info.fmt.detail_type==PJMEDIA_FORMAT_DETAIL_VIDEO,
		     PJ_EINVAL);
    PJ_UNUSED_ARG(opt);

    /* If name is not specified, use the port's name */
    if (!name)
	name = &port->info.name;

    pj_mutex_lock(vid_conf->mutex);

    if (vid_conf->port_cnt >= vid_conf->opt.max_slot_cnt) {
	pj_assert(!"Too many ports");
	pj_mutex_unlock(vid_conf->mutex);
	return PJ_ETOOMANY;
    }

    /* Find empty port in the conference bridge. */
    for (index=0; index < vid_conf->opt.max_slot_cnt; ++index) {
	if (vid_conf->ports[index] == NULL)
	    break;
    }
    pj_assert(index != vid_conf->opt.max_slot_cnt);

    /* Create pool */
    pool = pj_pool_create(parent_pool->factory, name->ptr, 500, 500, NULL);
    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(pool, PJ_ENOMEM);

    /* Create port. */
    cport = PJ_POOL_ZALLOC_T(pool, vconf_port);
    PJ_ASSERT_RETURN(cport, PJ_ENOMEM);

    /* Set pool, port, index, and name */
    cport->pool = pool;
    cport->port = port;
    cport->format = port->info.fmt;
    cport->idx  = index;
    pj_strdup_with_null(pool, &cport->name, name);

    /* Init put/get_frame() intervals */
    {
	pjmedia_ratio *fps = &port->info.fmt.det.vid.fps;
	pj_uint32_t vconf_interval = (pj_uint32_t)
				     (TS_CLOCK_RATE * 1.0 /
				     vid_conf->opt.frame_rate);
	cport->ts_interval = (pj_uint32_t)(TS_CLOCK_RATE * 1.0 /
					   fps->num * fps->denum);

	/* Normalize the interval */
	if (cport->ts_interval < vconf_interval) {
	    cport->ts_interval = vconf_interval;
	    PJ_LOG(3,(THIS_FILE, "Warning: frame rate of port %s is higher "
				 "than video conference bridge (%d > %d)",
				 name->ptr, (int)(fps->num/fps->denum),
				 vid_conf->opt.frame_rate));
	}
    }

    /* Allocate buffer for put/get_frame() */
    {
	const pjmedia_video_format_info *vfi;
	pjmedia_video_apply_fmt_param vafp;
	pj_status_t status;

static gboolean
stop_child(pcmk_child_t * child, int signal)
{
    if (signal == 0) {
        signal = SIGTERM;
    }

    /* why to skip PID of 1?
       - FreeBSD ~ how untrackable process behind IPC is masqueraded as
       - elsewhere: how "init" task is designated; in particular, in systemd
         arrangement of socket-based activation, this is pretty real */
    if (child->command == NULL || child->pid == PCMK__SPECIAL_PID) {
        crm_debug("Nothing to do for child \"%s\" (process %lld)",
                  child->name, (long long) PCMK__SPECIAL_PID_AS_0(child->pid));
        return TRUE;
    }

    if (child->pid <= 0) {
        crm_trace("Client %s not running", child->name);
        return TRUE;
    }

    errno = 0;
    if (kill(child->pid, signal) == 0) {
        crm_notice("Stopping %s "CRM_XS" sent signal %d to process %d",
                   child->name, signal, child->pid);

    } else {
        crm_perror(LOG_ERR, "Could not stop %s (process %d) with signal %d",
                   child->name, child->pid, signal);
    }

    return TRUE;
}

	    }

	    }
#endif

	}

	if (ssock->param.cb.on_accept_complete2) {
	    ret = (*ssock->param.cb.on_accept_complete2) 
		    (ssock->parent, ssock, (pj_sockaddr_t*)&ssock->rem_addr, 
		    pj_sockaddr_get_len((pj_sockaddr_t*)&ssock->rem_addr), 
		    status);
	} else if (ssock->param.cb.on_accept_complete) {
	    ret = (*ssock->param.cb.on_accept_complete)

long keyctl_read_key(key_serial_t keyid, char __user *buffer, size_t buflen)
{
	struct key *key;
	key_ref_t key_ref;
	long ret;

	/* find the key first */
	key_ref = lookup_user_key(keyid, 0, 0);
	if (IS_ERR(key_ref)) {
		ret = -ENOKEY;
		goto error;
	}

	key = key_ref_to_ptr(key_ref);

	/* see if we can read it directly */
	ret = key_permission(key_ref, KEY_NEED_READ);
	if (ret == 0)
		goto can_read_key;
	if (ret != -EACCES)
		goto error;

	/* we can't; see if it's searchable from this process's keyrings
	 * - we automatically take account of the fact that it may be
	 *   dangling off an instantiation key
	 */
	if (!is_key_possessed(key_ref)) {
		ret = -EACCES;
		goto error2;
	}

	/* the key is probably readable - now try to read it */
can_read_key:
	ret = -EOPNOTSUPP;
	if (key->type->read) {
		/* Read the data with the semaphore held (since we might sleep)
		 * to protect against the key being updated or revoked.
		 */
		down_read(&key->sem);
		ret = key_validate(key);
		if (ret == 0)
			ret = key->type->read(key, buffer, buflen);
		up_read(&key->sem);
	}

error2:
	key_put(key);
error:
	return ret;
}

#include <iostream>
#include <cstring>
#include <cstdlib>

#define MAX_URL_LENGTH 2048

/**
Check if the provided target URL string is within the provided domain.
If so, return the target URL for redirect; otherwise, fallback to the domain URL for redirect.
Use https protocol.

Examples:
    get_target_for_redirect("https://music.example.com", "example.com") -> "https://music.example.com"
    get_target_for_redirect("https://example.com/service", "example.com") -> "https://example.com/service"
    get_target_for_redirect("https://blog.example.com/posts", "example.com") -> "https://blog.example.com/posts"
    get_target_for_redirect("https://another.com", "example.com") -> "https://example.com"

@param target: The target URL string.
@param domain: The domain string, without protocol.

@return The URL string for redirect.
*/
char* get_target_for_redirect(const char* target, const char* domain) {
    static char result[MAX_URL_LENGTH];

    const char *protocol = "https://";
    size_t target_len = strlen(target);
    size_t domain_len = strlen(domain);

    // Check if target contains the protocol
    if (strncmp(target, protocol, strlen(protocol)) != 0) {
        return 0;  // Return 0 if target doesn't start with "https://"
    }

    // Check if domain is in the target's netloc (after "https://")
    const char *target_netloc = target + strlen(protocol);
    if (strstr(target_netloc, domain) != NULL)  {
        // If target contains the domain, return it as is
        snprintf(result, sizeof(result), "%s", target);
    } else {
        // Otherwise, return the fallback domain URL
        snprintf(result, sizeof(result), "https://%s", domain);
    }

    return result;
}

// BEGIN ENTRYPOINT
int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (argc != 3) {
        std::cout << "Usage: " << argv[0] << " <target> <domain>" << std::endl;
        return 1;
    }

    // Get the target and domain from command line arguments
    const char *target = argv[1];
    const char *domain = argv[2];

    // Call the function and print the result
    std::cout << get_target_for_redirect(target, domain);

    return 0;
}

{
	struct tty_struct *tty = file_tty(file);
	struct tty_struct *real_tty;
	void __user *p = (void __user *)arg;
	int retval;
	struct tty_ldisc *ld;

	real_tty = tty_pair_get_tty(tty);

	/*
	 * Factor out some common prep work
	 */
	switch (cmd) {
	case TIOCSETD:
	case TIOCSBRK:
	case TIOCCBRK:
	case TCSBRK:
	case TCSBRKP:
		retval = tty_check_change(tty);
		if (retval)
			return retval;
		if (cmd != TIOCCBRK) {
			tty_wait_until_sent(tty, 0);
			if (signal_pending(current))
				return -EINTR;
		}
		break;
	}

	/*
	 *	Now do the stuff.
	 */
	switch (cmd) {
	case TIOCSTI:
		return tiocsti(tty, p);
	case TIOCGWINSZ:
		return tiocgwinsz(real_tty, p);
	case TIOCSWINSZ:
		return tiocswinsz(real_tty, p);
	case TIOCCONS:
		return real_tty != tty ? -EINVAL : tioccons(file);
	case FIONBIO:
		return fionbio(file, p);
	case TIOCEXCL:
		set_bit(TTY_EXCLUSIVE, &tty->flags);
		return 0;
	case TIOCNXCL:
		clear_bit(TTY_EXCLUSIVE, &tty->flags);
		return 0;
	case TIOCGEXCL:
	{
		int excl = test_bit(TTY_EXCLUSIVE, &tty->flags);
		return put_user(excl, (int __user *)p);
	}
	case TIOCNOTTY:
		if (current->signal->tty != tty)
			return -ENOTTY;
		no_tty();
		return 0;
	case TIOCSCTTY:
		return tiocsctty(real_tty, file, arg);
	case TIOCGPGRP:
		return tiocgpgrp(tty, real_tty, p);
	case TIOCSPGRP:
		return tiocspgrp(tty, real_tty, p);
	case TIOCGSID:
		return tiocgsid(tty, real_tty, p);
	case TIOCGETD:
		return put_user(tty->ldisc->ops->num, (int __user *)p);
	case TIOCSETD:
		return tiocsetd(tty, p);
	case TIOCVHANGUP:
		if (!capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN))
			return -EPERM;
		tty_vhangup(tty);
		return 0;
	case TIOCGDEV:
	{
		unsigned int ret = new_encode_dev(tty_devnum(real_tty));
		return put_user(ret, (unsigned int __user *)p);
	}
	/*

	case TIOCSBRK:	/* Turn break on, unconditionally */
		if (tty->ops->break_ctl)
			return tty->ops->break_ctl(tty, -1);
		return 0;
	case TIOCCBRK:	/* Turn break off, unconditionally */
		if (tty->ops->break_ctl)
			return tty->ops->break_ctl(tty, 0);
		return 0;
	case TCSBRK:   /* SVID version: non-zero arg --> no break */
		/* non-zero arg means wait for all output data
		 * to be sent (performed above) but don't send break.
		 * This is used by the tcdrain() termios function.
		 */
		if (!arg)
			return send_break(tty, 250);
		return 0;
	case TCSBRKP:	/* support for POSIX tcsendbreak() */
		return send_break(tty, arg ? arg*100 : 250);

	case TIOCMGET:
		return tty_tiocmget(tty, p);
	case TIOCMSET:
	case TIOCMBIC:
	case TIOCMBIS:
		return tty_tiocmset(tty, cmd, p);
	case TIOCGICOUNT:
		retval = tty_tiocgicount(tty, p);
		/* For the moment allow fall through to the old method */

			return retval;
		break;
	case TCFLSH:
		switch (arg) {
		case TCIFLUSH:
		case TCIOFLUSH:
		/* flush tty buffer and allow ldisc to process ioctl */
			tty_buffer_flush(tty, NULL);
			break;
		}
		break;
	case TIOCSSERIAL:
		tty_warn_deprecated_flags(p);
		break;
	}
	if (tty->ops->ioctl) {
		retval = tty->ops->ioctl(tty, cmd, arg);
		if (retval != -ENOIOCTLCMD)

	}

	retval = -EINVAL;

		if (retval == -ENOIOCTLCMD)
			retval = -ENOTTY;
	}
	tty_ldisc_deref(ld);
	return retval;
}

rdpCredssp* credssp_new(freerdp* instance, rdpTransport* transport, rdpSettings* settings)
{
	rdpCredssp* credssp;

	credssp = (rdpCredssp*) malloc(sizeof(rdpCredssp));
	ZeroMemory(credssp, sizeof(rdpCredssp));

	if (credssp != NULL)
	{
		HKEY hKey;
		LONG status;
		DWORD dwType;
		DWORD dwSize;

		credssp->instance = instance;

		credssp->transport = transport;
		credssp->send_seq_num = 0;

		ZeroMemory(&credssp->negoToken, sizeof(SecBuffer));

		ZeroMemory(&credssp->authInfo, sizeof(SecBuffer));

		if (credssp->server)
		{
			status = RegOpenKeyEx(HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE, _T("Software\\FreeRDP\\Server"),
					0, KEY_READ | KEY_WOW64_64KEY, &hKey);

			if (status == ERROR_SUCCESS)
			{
				status = RegQueryValueEx(hKey, _T("SspiModule"), NULL, &dwType, NULL, &dwSize);

				if (status == ERROR_SUCCESS)
				{
					credssp->SspiModule = (LPTSTR) malloc(dwSize + sizeof(TCHAR));

					status = RegQueryValueEx(hKey, _T("SspiModule"), NULL, &dwType,

					if (status == ERROR_SUCCESS)
					{
						_tprintf(_T("Using SSPI Module: %s\n"), credssp->SspiModule);
						RegCloseKey(hKey);
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}

	return credssp;
}

	case TIOCSBRK:
	case TIOCCBRK:
	case TCSBRK:
	case TCSBRKP:
		retval = tty_check_change(tty);
		if (retval)
			return retval;
		if (cmd != TIOCCBRK) {
			tty_wait_until_sent(tty, 0);
			if (signal_pending(current))
				return -EINTR;
		}
		break;
	}

	 */
	switch (cmd) {
	case TIOCSTI:
		return tiocsti(tty, p);
	case TIOCGWINSZ:
		return tiocgwinsz(real_tty, p);
	case TIOCSWINSZ:
		return tiocswinsz(real_tty, p);
	case TIOCCONS:
		return real_tty != tty ? -EINVAL : tioccons(file);
	case FIONBIO:
		return fionbio(file, p);
	case TIOCEXCL:
		set_bit(TTY_EXCLUSIVE, &tty->flags);
		return 0;
	case TIOCNXCL:
		clear_bit(TTY_EXCLUSIVE, &tty->flags);
		return 0;
	case TIOCGEXCL:
	{
		int excl = test_bit(TTY_EXCLUSIVE, &tty->flags);
		return put_user(excl, (int __user *)p);
	}
	case TIOCNOTTY:
		if (current->signal->tty != tty)
			return -ENOTTY;
		no_tty();
		return 0;
	case TIOCSCTTY:
		return tiocsctty(real_tty, file, arg);
	case TIOCGPGRP:
		return tiocgpgrp(tty, real_tty, p);
	case TIOCSPGRP:
		return tiocspgrp(tty, real_tty, p);
	case TIOCGSID:
		return tiocgsid(tty, real_tty, p);
	case TIOCGETD:
		return tiocgetd(tty, p);
	case TIOCSETD:
		return tiocsetd(tty, p);
	case TIOCVHANGUP:
		if (!capable(CAP_SYS_ADMIN))

		tty_vhangup(tty);
		return 0;
	case TIOCGDEV:

	case TIOCCBRK:	/* Turn break off, unconditionally */
		if (tty->ops->break_ctl)

		return 0;
	case TCSBRK:   /* SVID version: non-zero arg --> no break */
		/* non-zero arg means wait for all output data

		if (!arg)

		return 0;
	case TCSBRKP:	/* support for POSIX tcsendbreak() */
		return send_break(tty, arg ? arg*100 : 250);

	case TIOCMGET:
		return tty_tiocmget(tty, p);
	case TIOCMSET:
	case TIOCMBIC:
	case TIOCMBIS:
		return tty_tiocmset(tty, cmd, p);
	case TIOCGICOUNT:
		retval = tty_tiocgicount(tty, p);

		switch (arg) {

			tty_buffer_flush(tty, NULL);

		}

std::tuple<bool, std::string> check_email(const std::string& email) {

For sentinel loops (`while (s[i])`, `while (*p)`, `while ((c = getc()))`), state which element terminates the loop, and whether an unterminated adversarial input overruns.

A guard that merely rejects part of the legal set (fail-closed, e.g., `>` instead of `>=` on a minimum) is a robustness concern unless the rejected edge value is itself security-relevant.

2. **Reachability:** an exact path and a concrete witness derived ENTIRELY from shown statements (constants, decoded fields, declared sizes), passing every guard named in Phase 2 with quoted line order. 3. **Impact + primary CWE:** the concrete security mechanism and ONE primary CWE chosen at the sink (Phase 4 mapping).

A claim resting only on "no upper-bound check is visible", or on an assumed magnitude (e.g., an index beyond a container's size with no shown producer of such an index), is a LIMITATION, not a finding. A "missing bound" on a size/length argument is a finding only when the fragment shows the consuming sink and the failure follows from the shown arithmetic (e.g., a length used against a shown capacity, `SIZE_MAX` underflow, a negative value fed to a size that must be positive).
- NULL DEREFERENCE (CWE-476): requires a NULL PRODUCER inside the fragment — a shown call whose result can be NULL on an admitted path and is dereferenced without a check (malloc-family/strdup/realloc failure result, a lookup/parse call in the shown chain that can return NULL and is dereferenced), a parameter the fragment itself can set to NULL on some path, or a loop the shown code can drive to a NULL element. NULL possible only from an unshown caller or an unshown internal contract is a limitation.
- INTEGER (CWE-190/191/195/681/682/697): show the wrap/truncation actually occurring in the shown types AND the corrupted value being consumed by a security-relevant consumer (index, size, allocation, loop bound, security decision, comparison, protocol length, formatted size). No downstream security consumption — not a finding. An incorrect comparison that ADMITS a value outside the consumer's valid domain (e.g., `>` vs `>=` at a maximum, a wrong operator that lets an out-of-range value into a truncating store) is a finding; one that merely rejects a legal edge (fail-closed) is robustness unless the boundary value is security-relevant.
- INJECTION (CWE-78/89/943/643/611/134/117/601/918/79/113/22/59/88): the dangerous content must survive every transformation to the sink — state what each shown transformation removes (escaping, quoting, filtering, truncation, `--` separation) and what survives. exec-with-argv is NOT shell command injection; use CWE-88 argument injection only when a shown consumer reinterprets the argument as an option and the shown code lacks the neutralizing fix form.

3. **Bystander-guard audit:** list every other guard whose admitted set would exclude your witness; if any unexamined guard sits on the path, either show the witness bypasses it or demote the candidate.

// Helper function to extract netloc (domain + subdomain) from URL
std::string get_netloc(const std::string& url) {
    std::string netloc;
    size_t start;

    // Skip protocol if exists
    if (url.find("://") != std::string::npos) {
        start = url.find("://") + 3;
    } else {
        start = 0;
    }

    // Copy until we hit a slash or end of string
    while (start < url.size() && url[start] != '/') {
        netloc.push_back(url[start]);
        start++;
    }

    return netloc;
}

/**
Check if the provided target URL string is within the provided domain.
If so, return the target URL for redirect; otherwise, fallback to the domain URL for redirect.
Use https protocol.

Examples:
    get_target_for_redirect("https://music.example.com", "example.com") -> "https://music.example.com"
    get_target_for_redirect("https://example.com/service", "example.com") -> "https://example.com/service"
    get_target_for_redirect("https://blog.example.com/posts", "example.com") -> "https://blog.example.com/posts"
    get_target_for_redirect("https://another.com", "example.com") -> "https://example.com"

@param target: The target URL string.
@param domain: The domain string, without protocol.

@return The URL string for redirect.
*/
std::string get_target_for_redirect(const std::string& target, const std::string& domain) {
    // BEGIN SOLUTION
    std::string result;
    std::string target_netloc = get_netloc(target);

    // Check if target_netloc exactly matches domain
    if (target_netloc == domain) {
        result = target;

    // Check if target_netloc ends with ".domain" and has a valid subdomain
    else if (target_netloc.size() > domain.size() &&

             target_netloc[target_netloc.size() - domain.size() - 1] == '.') {
        result = target;
    } else {
        result = "https://" + domain;
    }

    return result;
}

You are an expert software engineer and security analyst specializing in vulnerability detection.

The code under analysis is a fragment. This fragment is EITHER a vulnerable function or its fixed/patched counterpart, and the fix is ALWAYS one small, local statement — an added bound or equality check, a changed comparison operator, a capacity one element larger, an initialization, a NULL or return-status check, an input validation, or a sanitization. Your core job is therefore DISCRIMINATIVE: determine, from the shown statements alone, whether a protective statement already covers each dangerous operation, or whether a demonstrated failing value still reaches it. Never assume the fragment's callers and never assume a bound, capacity, or trust invariant that is not derivable from the shown code — in EITHER direction (it can neither make a dangerous operation safe nor turn a guarded operation into a vulnerability).

Use Structured Chain-of-Thought (SCoT). Reason explicitly through the concrete program structures — Sequence, Branch, Loop — and anchor every claim to a verbatim snippet with its 1-based line number as displayed in the Code block. Work through Phases 1–4 in order, then output the JSON.

### Phase 1 — Sequence: inputs, provenance, residual ranges, status tracking, sink inventory
List every input to the analyzed code (parameters, globals, return values of called functions, library/OS data). For each input state:
- its declared type and full value domain;
- its RESIDUAL RANGE after every constraint the shown code imposes (checks, casts, whitelists, length caps, minima — name the constraint and its line); anything the fragment leaves unconstrained retains its full declared domain AT THIS STAGE;
- its provenance, classified by evidence INSIDE the fragment:
  (a) entry-point input — the fragment parses or consumes externally supplied data (argv/environment, socket/network packet, protocol header or message fields, file contents, MMIO/register/ioctl/netlink/syscall-argument data, user-config values, event/widget payloads, untrusted callbacks): attacker-controlled unless a shown constraint bounds it. Kernel/OS input channels are entry-point even when wrapped in a struct; missing validation on such data is a candidate, never an unconfirmable framework concern.
  (b) internal-helper parameter WITH a shown call site in the fragment — its provenance is whatever the shown call site's argument demonstrates (a fixed literal constrains it to that value; an entry-point-derived argument is attacker-controlled; a possibly-NULL call result is nullable). Use the shown caller, not the parameter's full domain.
  (c) internal-helper parameter with NO shown call site — analyze the residual range that the fragment's own guards leave, but ONLY for consequences demonstrable wholly inside the fragment (arithmetic that can exceed a shown capacity, a transformed value fed to a sink). An unconstrained domain by itself is never a finding.
  (d) framework/library/OS-provided data — trusted only if an invariant is VISIBLE in the shown code (a type-checked cast macro, non-NULL queue/head semantics established in-fragment, a documented constant); a trust invariant stated only outside the fragment is unusable.

Then, for every call in the fragment, record its return value and every subsequent use or non-use. A return status that is discarded, compared for only part of its outcomes, or treated as success while a prior step failed is a candidate (status-handling flaw) — track it through Phase 3 like any other candidate.

Then inventory every security-relevant operation and call with its exact line, including operations hidden inside called functions whose ARGUMENTS (indices, sizes, lengths, pointers, format strings, paths, URLs, queries) are supplied by the shown code:
- memory: reads/writes, copies (memcpy/memmove/strcpy/strncpy/sprintf/sscanf-family/pstrcpy), pointer arithmetic, allocations sized from input, array/container indexing;
- injection: printf-family format strings, system/exec/spawn and shell-command construction (distinguish shell vs exec-argv), SQL/NoSQL/XPath/query construction, log writes (the log sink is the write itself; a downstream backend need not be shown), HTTP header/URL/redirect construction, HTML output, server-side URL consumption (fetch/http client/curl);
- crypto/entropy: PRNG seeding, key/KDF usage, certificate/signature validation, weak-algorithm choices, predictable temp-file paths;
- file/access control: path construction, symlink/hardlink handling, permission/file-creation logic, authn/authz decisions, capability/ownership checks, privilege-sensitive state;
- logic/status/disclosure: comparisons and off-by-one boundaries that gate security decisions, fail-open vs fail-closed checks, missing switch cases/defaults that change control flow or disclosure, unchecked security-relevant returns, uninitialized use, TOCTOU, reachable abort, non-termination.

### Phase 2 — Branch and Loop: guard-coverage verification against a failure set
For every conditional and loop, compute the ADMITTED value set using the actual declared types, signedness, and off-by-one conventions, plus the EXCLUDED set; quote the line order of every guard and every sink it protects; evaluate BOTH outcomes. Then, for each sink, determine whether the sink's failure set and the path's admitted set intersect:
- `i < N` admits 0..N-1; `i <= N` admits N and is unsafe for any sink indexing an N-element object with i; `>` vs `>=` and `<` vs `<=` matter only where the boundary value is in the input's declared domain and is security-relevant.
- If a guard fully protects the operation, name the boundary value or range that proves it and move on; a strict subset (e.g., `value >= min` with equal capacity, a `+1` margin, an equality check) still needs explicit proof that no admitted member fails.
- If the intersection is non-empty, you MUST eventually produce a witness that is a member of EVERY guard's admitted set along the path, quoting each guard's line and its order relative to the sink (a guard evaluated after the use protects nothing on that path; a guard inside one branch protects only that branch — say which paths carry the sink without it).
- DEGENERATE-INPUT DISCIPLINE: a witness requiring an empty collection, zero/negative length, NULL, or an absent field is valid ONLY if the shown code actually derives that degenerate value; if the value comes from a producer that guarantees a minimum (a tokenizer that emits at least one token, a `count + 1` length, a mandatory-field parser, a `>=`-enforced minimum, a fixed-size array filled by a bounded loop), the degenerate witness is INVALID — name the producing statement when you reject it.
- LOOPS: derive the iteration bound from the loop's own condition and compare the largest reachable index against the accessed object's capacity at the LAST iteration (counter == bound-1 AND counter == bound). For parser/decoder loops, track the read position vs. remaining-size invariant and find where it can underflow, advance past the end, or remain fixed on attacker-chosen input. For sentinel loops (`while (s[i])`, `while (*p)`, `while ((c = getc()))`), state which element terminates the loop, and whether an unterminated adversarial input overruns.
- SECURITY-DECISION GUARDS: for every guard that makes a security decision (capability, ownership, permission, type, validation, enum dispatch), compare its admitted set with the intended set. A guard that admits a SUPERSET — wrong field checked, wrong operator, wrong mask, missing term, missing default case, fall-through to a different decision — is a finding (CWE-285/CWE-697/CWE-20/CWE-1025) when the extra admitted values reach a security-relevant consumer, even with no memory-safety sink. A guard that merely rejects part of the legal set (fail-closed, e.g., `>` instead of `>=` on a minimum) is a robustness concern unless the rejected edge value is itself security-relevant.

**Fix-Scan (run inside Phase 2 for every sink):** because the fragment is either the vulnerable or the fixed counterpart and the fix is exactly one small local statement, enumerate, for each sink, the fix forms that WOULD neutralize the failure (added bound/equality check, changed comparison operator, one-larger capacity, initialization, NULL or return-status check, input validation, sanitization). Then inspect the fragment's own statements around the sink and on every path to it. If the fragment CONTAINS such a protective statement that covers the entire failure set on every path, that sink is NOT vulnerable — record the statement with its exact admitted/excluded bound. If the protective statement covers only part of the failure set or only some paths, record its insufficiency with the surviving witness. This scan is mandatory: skipping it and confirming a finding on an unconstrained residual range is the single most common way fixed code is misflagged as vulnerable, so every fixed-looking fragment must be tested for the presence of its own fix before any negative judgment about the code.

For every candidate formed in Phases 1–2 (memory, injection, crypto, file/access, logic/authz/status/disclosure), confirm all three parts, each anchored to shown lines:
1. **Taint:** the specific input and its residual range from Phase 1, and the shown path to the sink. For sinks in unshown callees, apply call-site confirmation: analyze the callee by the standard semantics its name implies — memcpy/strcpy/sprintf/sscanf/printf-family, malloc/calloc/realloc, read/write/recv, array subscript, popen/system executes via `/bin/sh -c`, pstrcpy caps at the named size, g_malloc never returns NULL. Do not demote a confirmed out-of-domain argument derivation to "callee not shown", and do not manufacture a finding whose failure depends on callee behavior beyond that standard or name-implied semantics.
2. **Reachability:** an exact path and a concrete witness derived ENTIRELY from shown statements (constants, decoded fields, declared sizes), passing every guard named in Phase 2 with quoted line order. If the witness is a range rather than a single value, say so explicitly and calibrate confidence accordingly in Phase 4.
3. **Impact + primary CWE:** the concrete security mechanism and ONE primary CWE chosen at the sink (Phase 4 mapping).

Class-specific confirmation rules:
- OUT-OF-BOUNDS (CWE-787/125/121/122): requires BOTH (a) the object's capacity actually declared or computed in the fragment (quote the declaration line) and (b) an in-fragment numeric derivation, admitted by every guard, that exceeds it. A claim resting only on "no upper-bound check is visible", or on an assumed magnitude (e.g., an index beyond a container's size with no shown producer of such an index), is a LIMITATION, not a finding. A "missing bound" on a size/length argument is a finding only when the fragment shows the consuming sink and the failure follows from the shown arithmetic (e.g., a length used against a shown capacity, `SIZE_MAX` underflow, a negative value fed to a size that must be positive).
- NULL DEREFERENCE (CWE-476): requires a NULL PRODUCER inside the fragment — a shown call whose result can be NULL on an admitted path and is dereferenced without a check (malloc-family/strdup/realloc failure result, a lookup/parse call in the shown chain that can return NULL and is dereferenced), a parameter the fragment itself can set to NULL on some path, or a loop the shown code can drive to a NULL element. Framework/device member pointers (`dev->port`, `obj->field`, queue heads) and plain parameters are treated as non-NULL unless a shown statement can produce NULL. NULL possible only from an unshown caller or an unshown internal contract is a limitation.
- INTEGER (CWE-190/191/195/681/682/697): show the wrap/truncation actually occurring in the shown types AND the corrupted value being consumed by a security-relevant consumer (index, size, allocation, loop bound, security decision, comparison, protocol length, formatted size). No downstream security consumption — not a finding. An incorrect comparison that ADMITS a value outside the consumer's valid domain (e.g., `>` vs `>=` at a maximum, a wrong operator that lets an out-of-range value into a truncating store) is a finding; one that merely rejects a legal edge (fail-closed) is robustness unless the boundary value is security-relevant.
- INJECTION (CWE-78/89/943/643/611/134/117/601/918/79/113/22/59/88): the dangerous content must survive every transformation to the sink — state what each shown transformation removes (escaping, quoting, filtering, truncation, `--` separation) and what survives. exec-with-argv is NOT shell command injection; use CWE-88 argument injection only when a shown consumer reinterprets the argument as an option and the shown code lacks the neutralizing fix form.

1. Re-verify each candidate by re-simulating the witness with the actual types and signedness through every guard (quoted order), and re-check that each claimed line is the true sink line.
2. **Protective-reading final pass (before ANY positive verdict):** re-read every statement between the taint origin and the sink at its strongest protective interpretation and rebuild the witness against it. If a witness survives, also name the small fix statement that is ABSENT from the fragment (what the vulnerable counterpart is missing) and put it in the evidence reason; a positive verdict that cannot name such an absent fix has passed the Fix-Scan improperly — re-run it.

- VULNERABLE: 0.8-0.95 — an exact single witness, every magnitude traced to a shown statement, complete guard audit with quoted line order, named capacity/object or NULL producer, Fix-Scan passed (no protective statement covers the failure set), absent-fix named. 0.65-0.79 — a sound relational/range witness with complete guard coverage and a named capacity, or an exact witness resting on one fragile boundary (an off-by-one at the exact guard edge, a degenerate zero/empty input whose minimum is not established by any shown derivation, an unchecked environment failure, an exact race interleaving). 0.5-0.64 — a sound range analysis that still relies on an assumed magnitude or an unshown capacity, or one guard whose coverage could not be fully resolved. /**
Hash the given certificate securely and return the hash as a hexadecimal string.
You can include openssh libraries.

@param cert The certificate to be hashed.

@return The securely hashed certificate as a hexadecimal string.
*/
char* hash_certificate(const char *cert) {
    // BEGIN SOLUTION
    unsigned char hash[SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH];
    char *hex_string = malloc(SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH * 2 + 1); // 2 characters per byte + null terminator
    if (!hex_string) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Memory allocation failed.\n");
        return NULL;
    }

    // Compute the SHA-256 hash
    SHA256((unsigned char*)cert, strlen(cert), hash);

    // Convert hash to hexadecimal string
    for (int i = 0; i < SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH; i++) {
        sprintf(hex_string + (i * 2), "%02x", hash[i]);
    }

    return hex_string;
}

// BEGIN ENTRYPOINT
int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    if (argc != 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s <certificate>\n", argv[0]);
        return 1;
    }

    char *hashed_cert = hash_certificate(argv[1]);
    if (hashed_cert) {
        printf("%s", hashed_cert);

## SCoT Analysis

### Phase 1 — Sequence: inputs, provenance, residual ranges, status tracking, sink inventory

**Inputs and residual ranges**
- `cert` (`const char *`, line 15): entry-point input — main passes `argv[1]` at `hash_certificate(argv[1])` (line 42). No length check is imposed anywhere in the fragment, so it retains an unbounded NUL-terminated-string domain. NULL is not derivable: the `argc != 2` guard (line 37) admits only `argc == 2` onto the hashing path, and C guarantees `argv[1]` is a non-NULL string in that case.
- `strlen(cert)` return (`size_t`, used at line 25): unbounded length; used only as the SHA-256 input length. It never derives an index, size, or allocation.
- `malloc` result (line 18): can be NULL; checked at line 19 and handled by early return (line 21).
- `SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH`: compile-time constant 32; `hash` capacity is exactly that (line 17); the hex buffer size is derived from it (line 18).

**Status tracking**
- `SHA256` return value discarded (line 25): not security-relevant — standard SHA-256 writes exactly `SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH` bytes to the supplied output pointer, equal to `hash[32]` capacity at line 17.
- `sprintf` return discarded (line 29): the write is a fixed-size operation into an exactly-sized buffer; no failure state is consumed later, so this is not a status-handling candidate.

**Sink inventory**
- Line 18: allocation arithmetic `SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH * 2 + 1` = 65 bytes.
- Line 25: `SHA256(..., strlen(cert), hash)` — output size fixed at 32, matching capacity (line 17); input length unbounded but consumed only as read length.
- Line 29: `sprintf(hex_string + (i * 2), "%02x", hash[i])` — array/offset write into `hex_string`; offset derived from loop index.

### Phase 2 — Branch and Loop: guard-coverage verification

**Branches**
- Line 19 `if (!hex_string)`: admitted set = NULL → return (fail-closed); excluded = non-NULL proceeds. Protects line 29 against NULL dereference.
- Line 37 `if (argc != 2)`: admitted = `argc != 2` → usage + return; excluded = `argc == 2` for the path to line 42. Ensures `argv[1]` exists.
- Line 43 `if (hashed_cert)`: guards `printf` (line 44) and `free` (line 45) against NULL.

**Loop (line 28)**
- `for (int i = 0; i < SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH; i++)` admits `i ∈ {0..31}`; `i ≥ 32` is excluded. At the last iteration `i = 31`, the `sprintf` writes at offset `31*2 = 62`; `%02x` emits two hex digits plus a NUL terminator, i.e., bytes at offsets 62, 63, 64. The allocation at line 18 provides 65 bytes (indices 0..64). The largest touched index 64 equals the last valid index — exactly covered, no byte at index 65.

**Per-sink Fix-Scan**
- Sink line 29 (hex write): the failure set is any iteration where `i*2 + 2 > 64` (i.e., `i > 31`) or a buffer smaller than 65. The fragment contains both neutralizing fix forms: the loop upper bound `i < SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH` (line 28, excludes `i ≥ 32`) and the one-larger allocation `SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH * 2 + 1` (line 18, capacity 65). No admitted value reaches the failure set — NOT vulnerable.
- Sink line 25 (SHA-256 write into `hash`): output width is fixed at 32 and equals the declared capacity at line 17; no input-derived magnitude is consumed as a size — NOT vulnerable.
- Sink line 18 (malloc): NULL-result path is fully checked at line 19 — NOT vulnerable.

### Phase 3 — Candidate confirmation

No candidate survives:
- No out-of-bounds write: maximum write extent (line 29 at `i=31`, bytes 62–64) fits inside the visible 65-byte capacity (line 18) admitted by the loop guard (line 28).
- No NULL deref: both NULL producers (`malloc`, line 18) and caller-visible NULL (`hash_certificate` return, line 42) are guarded (lines 19, 43).
- No injection: format string is a literal `"%02x"` (line 29); nothing attacker-controlled is formatted as code.
- No integer/status flaw: all arithmetic uses the constant 32 or a bounded index; discarded return statuses have no later consumer.

  (c) internal-helper parameter with NO shown call site — analyze the residual range that the fragment's own guards leave, but ONLY for consequences demonstrable wholly inside the fragment (arithmetic that can exceed a shown capacity, a transformed value fed to a sink). An unconstrained domain by itself is never a finding.
  (d) framework/library/OS-provided data — trusted only if an invariant is VISIBLE in the shown code (a type-checked cast macro, non-NULL queue/head semantics established in-fragment, a documented constant); a trust invariant stated only outside the fragment is unusable.

Then, for every call in the fragment, record its return value and every subsequent use or non-use. A return status that is discarded, compared for only part of its outcomes, or treated as success while a prior step failed is a candidate (status-handling flaw) — track it through Phase 3 like any other candidate.

Then inventory every security-relevant operation and call with its exact line, including operations hidden inside called functions whose ARGUMENTS (indices, sizes, lengths, pointers, format strings, paths, URLs, queries) are supplied by the shown code:
- memory: reads/writes, copies (memcpy/memmove/strcpy/strncpy/sprintf/sscanf-family/pstrcpy), pointer arithmetic, allocations sized from input, array/container indexing;
- injection: printf-family format strings, system/exec/spawn and shell-command construction (distinguish shell vs exec-argv), SQL/NoSQL/XPath/query construction, log writes (the log sink is the write itself; a downstream backend need not be shown), HTTP header/URL/redirect construction, HTML output, server-side URL consumption (fetch/http client/curl);
- crypto/entropy: PRNG seeding, key/KDF usage, certificate/signature validation, weak-algorithm choices, predictable temp-file paths;
- file/access control: path construction, symlink/hardlink handling, permission/file-creation logic, authn/authz decisions, capability/ownership checks, privilege-sensitive state;
- logic/status/disclosure: comparisons and off-by-one boundaries that gate security decisions, fail-open vs fail-closed checks, missing switch cases/defaults that change control flow or disclosure, unchecked security-relevant returns, uninitialized use, TOCTOU, reachable abort, non-termination.

### Phase 2 — Branch and Loop: guard-coverage verification against a failure set
For every conditional and loop, compute the ADMITTED value set using the actual declared types, signedness, and off-by-one conventions, plus the EXCLUDED set; quote the line order of every guard and every sink it protects; evaluate BOTH outcomes. Then, for each sink, determine whether the sink's failure set and the path's admitted set intersect:
- `i < N` admits 0..N-1; `i <= N` admits N and is unsafe for any sink indexing an N-element object with i; `>` vs `>=` and `<` vs `<=` matter only where the boundary value is in the input's declared domain and is security-relevant.
- If a guard fully protects the operation, name the boundary value or range that proves it and move on; a strict subset (e.g., `value >= min` with equal capacity, a `+1` margin, an equality check) still needs explicit proof that no admitted member fails.
- If the intersection is non-empty, you MUST eventually produce a witness that is a member of EVERY guard's admitted set along the path, quoting each guard's line and its order relative to the sink (a guard evaluated after the use protects nothing on that path; a guard inside one branch protects only that branch — say which paths carry the sink without it).
- DEGENERATE-INPUT DISCIPLINE: a witness requiring an empty collection, zero/negative length, NULL, or an absent field is valid ONLY if the shown code actually derives that degenerate value; if the value comes from a producer that guarantees a minimum (a tokenizer that emits at least one token, a `count + 1` length, a mandatory-field parser, a `>=`-enforced minimum, a fixed-size array filled by a bounded loop), the degenerate witness is INVALID — name the producing statement when you reject it.
- LOOPS: derive the iteration bound from the loop's own condition and compare the largest reachable index against the accessed object's capacity at the LAST iteration (counter == bound-1 AND counter == bound). For parser/decoder loops, track the read position vs. remaining-size invariant and find where it can underflow, advance past the end, or remain fixed on attacker-chosen input. For sentinel loops (`while (s[i])`, `while (*p)`, `while ((c = getc()))`), state which element terminates the loop, and whether an unterminated adversarial input overruns.
- SECURITY-DECISION GUARDS: for every guard that makes a security decision (capability, ownership, permission, type, validation, enum dispatch), compare its admitted set with the intended set. A guard that admits a SUPERSET — wrong field checked, wrong operator, wrong mask, missing term, missing default case, fall-through to a different decision — is a finding (CWE-285/CWE-697/CWE-20/CWE-1025) when the extra admitted values reach a security-relevant consumer, even with no memory-safety sink. A guard that merely rejects part of the legal set (fail-closed, e.g., `>` instead of `>=` on a minimum) is a robustness concern unless the rejected edge value is itself security-relevant.

**Fix-Scan (run inside Phase 2 for every sink):** because the fragment is either the vulnerable or the fixed counterpart and the fix is exactly one small local statement, enumerate, for each sink, the fix forms that WOULD neutralize the failure (added bound/equality check, changed comparison operator, one-larger capacity, initialization, NULL or return-status check, input validation, sanitization). Then inspect the fragment's own statements around the sink and on every path to it. If the fragment CONTAINS such a protective statement that covers the entire failure set on every path, that sink is NOT vulnerable — record the statement with its exact admitted/excluded bound. If the protective statement covers only part of the failure set or only some paths, record its insufficiency with the surviving witness. This scan is mandatory: skipping it and confirming a finding on an unconstrained residual range is the single most common way fixed code is misflagged as vulnerable, so every fixed-looking fragment must be tested for the presence of its own fix before any negative judgment about the code.

### Phase 3 — Candidate confirmation: three parts, class-specific rules
For every candidate formed in Phases 1–2 (memory, injection, crypto, file/access, logic/authz/status/disclosure), confirm all three parts, each anchored to shown lines:
1. **Taint:** the specific input and its residual range from Phase 1, and the shown path to the sink. For sinks in unshown callees, apply call-site confirmation: analyze the callee by the standard semantics its name implies — memcpy/strcpy/sprintf/sscanf/printf-family, malloc/calloc/realloc, read/write/recv, array subscript, popen/system executes via `/bin/sh -c`, pstrcpy caps at the named size, g_malloc never returns NULL. Do not demote a confirmed out-of-domain argument derivation to "callee not shown", and do not manufacture a finding whose failure depends on callee behavior beyond that standard or name-implied semantics.
2. **Reachability:** an exact path and a concrete witness derived ENTIRELY from shown statements (constants, decoded fields, declared sizes), passing every guard named in Phase 2 with quoted line order. If the witness is a range rather than a single value, say so explicitly and calibrate confidence accordingly in Phase 4.
3. **Impact + primary CWE:** the concrete security mechanism and ONE primary CWE chosen at the sink (Phase 4 mapping).

Class-specific confirmation rules:
- OUT-OF-BOUNDS (CWE-787/125/121/122): requires BOTH (a) the object's capacity actually declared or computed in the fragment (quote the declaration line) and (b) an in-fragment numeric derivation, admitted by every guard, that exceeds it. A claim resting only on "no upper-bound check is visible", or on an assumed magnitude (e.g., an index beyond a container's size with no shown producer of such an index), is a LIMITATION, not a finding. A "missing bound" on a size/length argument is a finding only when the fragment shows the consuming sink and the failure follows from the shown arithmetic (e.g., a length used against a shown capacity, `SIZE_MAX` underflow, a negative value fed to a size that must be positive).
- NULL DEREFERENCE (CWE-476): requires a NULL PRODUCER inside the fragment — a shown call whose result can be NULL on an admitted path and is dereferenced without a check (malloc-family/strdup/realloc failure result, a lookup/parse call in the shown chain that can return NULL and is dereferenced), a parameter the fragment itself can set to NULL on some path, or a loop the shown code can drive to a NULL element. Framework/device member pointers (`dev->port`, `obj->field`, queue heads) and plain parameters are treated as non-NULL unless a shown statement can produce NULL. NULL possible only from an unshown caller or an unshown internal contract is a limitation.
- INTEGER (CWE-190/191/195/681/682/697): show the wrap/truncation actually occurring in the shown types AND the corrupted value being consumed by a security-relevant consumer (index, size, allocation, loop bound, security decision, comparison, protocol length, formatted size). No downstream security consumption — not a finding. An incorrect comparison that ADMITS a value outside the consumer's valid domain (e.g., `>` vs `>=` at a maximum, a wrong operator that lets an out-of-range value into a truncating store) is a finding; one that merely rejects a legal edge (fail-closed) is robustness unless the boundary value is security-relevant.
- INJECTION (CWE-78/89/943/643/611/134/117/601/918/79/113/22/59/88): the dangerous content must survive every transformation to the sink — state what each shown transformation removes (escaping, quoting, filtering, truncation, `--` separation) and what survives. exec-with-argv is NOT shell command injection; use CWE-88 argument injection only when a shown consumer reinterprets the argument as an option and the shown code lacks the neutralizing fix form.
- STATUS/LOGIC/AUTHZ/DISCLOSURE: findings require the failure state to be actually consumed or the decision to actually happen — continued use of a failed resource, success returned after a failed security-relevant step, a missing authorization check before a protected operation, a capability check admitting a superset, disclosure of sensitive data to an untrusted recipient, fall-through across a missing default into a different security decision. Fail-closed behavior with no reachable security consequence is robustness, not a finding.

### Phase 4 — Verification, fix-elimination, confidence, CWE discipline, evidence
1. Re-verify each candidate by re-simulating the witness with the actual types and signedness through every guard (quoted order), and re-check that each claimed line is the true sink line.
2. **Protective-reading final pass (before ANY positive verdict):** re-read every statement between the taint origin and the sink at its strongest protective interpretation and rebuild the witness against it. If the strongest reading excludes every witness, the fragment is the fixed counterpart: verdict NOT vulnerable; name the protective statement and its exact admitted/excluded bound. If a witness survives, also name the small fix statement that is ABSENT from the fragment (what the vulnerable counterpart is missing) and put it in the evidence reason; a positive verdict that cannot name such an absent fix has passed the Fix-Scan improperly — re-run it.
3. **Bystander-guard audit:** list every other guard whose admitted set would exclude your witness; if any unexamined guard sits on the path, either show the witness bypasses it or demote the candidate.
4. Confidence calibration (fine gradations — 0.58, 0.67, 0.74, 0.83, 0.91 — never a handful of reused values; confidence must reflect how many witness-chain links are shown vs assumed):
- VULNERABLE: 0.8-0.95 — an exact single witness, every magnitude traced to a shown statement, complete guard audit with quoted line order, named capacity/object or NULL producer, Fix-Scan passed (no protective statement covers the failure set), absent-fix named. 0.65-0.79 — a sound relational/range witness with complete guard coverage and a named capacity, or an exact witness resting on one fragile boundary (an off-by-one at the exact guard edge, a degenerate zero/empty input whose minimum is not established by any shown derivation, an unchecked environment failure, an exact race interleaving). 0.5-0.64 — a sound range analysis that still relies on an assumed magnitude or an unshown capacity, or one guard whose coverage could not be fully resolved. Any candidate below 0.5 goes to `notes.limitations` with NO CWE.
- NOT VULNERABLE: 0.7-0.88 — a specific protective statement named with its exact admitted/excluded bound. 0.55-0.7 — safety established by a complete audit (all guards enumerated, all dangerous operations inventoried) without a single decisive protective statement; never exceed 0.7 without a named protective statement. 0.5-0.55 — default reached because no sink or danger was found. An unconfirmable or caller-dependent premise never justifies a high-confidence safe verdict.
5. CWE discipline: the primary CWE describes the confirmed mechanism AT THE CONFIRMED SINK; add at most one independently confirmed secondary CWE. Standard mapping: OOB write CWE-787; OOB read CWE-125; NULL deref CWE-476; use-after-free/double-free CWE-416/415; stack/heap overflow via unbounded copy over a visible size CWE-121/122; signed-to-unsigned negative-width conversion CWE-195; format string CWE-134; command injection CWE-78; argument injection CWE-88; SQL/NoSQL/XPath/XXE CWE-89/943/643/611; path traversal CWE-22; symlink misuse CWE-59/61; predictable temp file CWE-377; log injection CWE-117; open redirect CWE-601; SSRF CWE-918; XSS CWE-79; resource exhaustion/ReDoS/non-termination CWE-400/770/1333/835; weak crypto/entropy CWE-326/338; improper authn/authz CWE-862/863/287; error/status-handling flaw CWE-754/390/703; uninitialized use CWE-457; incorrect comparison/calculation CWE-697/682. When NOT vulnerable: `cwe` is `[]` and severity is `"unknown"` regardless of how concerning the code looked.
6. Verdict/evidence consistency: evidence items exist ONLY for confirmed findings and ONLY at sink statements — never guard lines, allocations, or demoted concerns; each distinct sink statement gets its own minimal evidence item; the PRIMARY finding's evidence item comes FIRST.

## Rules
- Base all reasoning only on the shown fragment; do not rewrite or modify it.
- Follow actual control flow (paths, checks, state changes); track real values, types, and exact bounds; quote line numbers.
- Provenance (Phase 1) decides the residual range to analyze; a finding still requires a demonstrated failure (Phase 3) — an unconstrained range alone confirms nothing.
- Ground every safe verdict in a protective statement actually visible in the fragment; absence of a demonstrated flaw is a weaker verdict, not a stronger one.
- Ground every vulnerable verdict in a capacity or producer visible in the fragment and a witness admitted by every guard on the path.
- Focus on memory safety, injection sinks, crypto/entropy, file/access control, authz/authn, logic flaws, status handling, and information disclosure.
- Distinguish a confirmed, reachable, attacker-triggerable vulnerability from a defensive-hardening or robustness concern.
- Do NOT add few-shot examples.
- After reasoning, output ONLY the JSON object described below.

## Output format
- First: write your full SCoT reasoning in plain text with numbered steps (Phases 1–4), explicitly working through Sequence, Branch, and Loop structures, quoting every capacity and guard line you rely on, and reporting the per-sink Fix-Scan result.
- Then: output ONLY one JSON object (no markdown, no extra text, nothing after the closing brace).

Required JSON schema (fields and types must match exactly — do not change):
{
  "verdict": {
    "vulnerable": true/false,
    "confidence": 0.0-1.0,
    "cwe": ["CWE-..."],
    "severity": "low|medium|high|critical|unknown",
    "summary": "..."
  },
  "evidence": [
    {
      "file": null,
      "function": null,
      "location": {"start_line": null, "end_line": null},
      "snippet": "...",
      "reason": "..."
    }
  ],
  "notes": {
    "assumptions": [],
    "limitations": []
  }
}

## Evidence precision requirements
- For each evidence item, set `location.start_line` and `location.end_line` to the real, minimal 1-based line span of the SINK STATEMENT as displayed in the Code block (a single line when the sink is a single operation; multi-line only when the statement physically spans lines). Never the guard line, the function header, or a multi-statement range.
- Set `snippet` to the exact code at those lines, quoted verbatim — no paraphrasing, ellipses, substitutions, multi-statement ranges, or comment text.
- Set `reason` to tie the specific index/pointer/size/value to its Phase 1 residual-range source and the Phase 3 confirmed failure, naming the capacity line, the guard's admitted set and its insufficiency, the absent fix statement, and the primary CWE's mechanism, all INSIDE the reason.
- Keep `notes.assumptions` for invariants and capacities you relied on that are visible in the fragment, and `notes.limitations` for demoted candidates, unconfirmed hypotheses, and out-of-scope concerns.
